findings.what_was_wrong: The Group column writes Media 751 times and media 5 times, so a case-sensitive count or filter (pandas, R, SQL) splits one group in two; all five lowercase rows are the guests whose occupation is 'news anchor' (Jeff Varner, Judy Woodruff twice, Candy Crowley, Bret Baier).

other_excerpt_flags: On the excerpt only, the engine also flags GoogleKnowlege_Occupation 'Journalist' (4 rows: sheet rows 3, 24, 36, 71) beside 'journalist' (8) and 'Singer-songwriter' (row 90) beside 'singer-songwriter' (5), Medium. Real too: the same occupation in two capitalisations (the full table has 61 occupations written two or more ways, e.g. journalist 180 / Journalist 72), but the full-table scan does not flag that column, so a website line about the full table should name only the Group finding.
row_numbering: Row numbers are sheet rows: the header is row 1, so data row k (counting from 1) is sheet row k + 1. source_sheet_row is the same row in the full published file.
